columns.text: The Saisonkalender is a Brandenburg cultural artifact, a printed calendar of what is actually growing in your region this month. The web carries dozens of "what's in season" pages. Few carry the same load. They do not distinguish Brandenburg field asparagus in May from Spanish hothouse asparagus in March, or note that a German greenhouse tomato in February has a worse carbon footprint than one shipped from Almería. To rebuild the Saisonkalender as interactive data is to keep the regional frame and make the supply chain that quietly replaced most of it visible underneath.

The first move is classification. 114 produce items are tracked across the calendar year at 365-day resolution and labelled with one of seven origin tiers per day, from Brandenburg open-field to non-EU import. Where the national BZfE calendar diverges from Brandenburg-specific sources, the Brandenburg-specific call wins. A radial wheel reads the year as cyclical. A 41,610-cell mosaic reads as a Du Bois plate, temporal grain as catalog. A specimen plate treats each item as an engineering schematic. A chord plot reads origin-flow as textile. A stratigraphic core reads time as depth. Hand-built in SVG and canvas. No charting library. The atlas is called Saisonkalender.
